ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a nitrogen molecule, N≡N, reacting with three hydrogen molecules, each shown as H-H. An arrow points to the products, which are two ammonia molecules, each with one N bonded to three H atoms. Reasoning: On the reactant side there are 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. On the product side, the two ammonia molecules together also contain 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Because the same number and kinds of atoms appear before and after the reaction, the total mass remains the same.
